- `Plugins/P3/**`

- production Experience boots and reaches gameplay without V1 gameplay bootstrap

- architecture guard from A0 remains green against the final tree

## 2026-09-02 final product integration contract

**Current status: NOT READY.** This issue now owns the continuously runnable default product and its readiness ledger. ÔÇ£No feature expansionÔÇØ means no unrelated scope invention; it does not forbid implementing missing composition or behavior required by the existing North Star.

### Required default-path ledger

| Domain | Minimum closure state |
| --- | --- |
| Default map/GameMode/Experience | clean project-default boot; exact Experience/PawnData recorded |
| Player identity, input, camera | normal semantic input and view modes on the default path |
| Avatar and animation | authored package hydrated/valid, selected, spawned, and locomoting |
| Interaction, inventory, persistence | core loop and save/session behavior composed |
| Combat, abilities, traversal, VFX | normal-input server-authoritative loop with required presentation |
| Construction and earthworks | costs, world/navigation interaction, persistence, and multiplayer authority |
| Survival and respawn | cross-domain defeat/respawn state on the same product path |
| RTS, Lane War, tower defense, AI | coherent playable loop with one runtime authority |
| World/environment | production world boots without V1 repair/bootstrap ownership |
| UI/read models | integrated product state without central HUD scanning/switchboard |
| Multiplayer/session | dedicated server plus two clients for required networked loops |
| Presentation/performance | inspected current-head flows and recorded baseline |
| V1 retirement | one named authority per migrated system; V1 is reference/test only |

Every row records owner, exact head, state (`ABSENT`, `IMPLEMENTED`, `SYSTEM_PROVEN`, `DEFAULT_PATH_PROVEN`), proof level, and first unmet gate. Only `DEFAULT_PATH_PROVEN` satisfies this issue.

### Pull order and proof discipline

- Pull the oldest blocked default-path row; do not open more horizontal lanes while WIP or branch age rises.
- Validate LFS hydration, Primary Asset resolution, soft dependencies, authored metadata, and package loadability before build/runtime admission.
- Use one stable verifier and one default-product smoke per meaningful exact head.
- After the first exact failure, retry only after naming the source/content/environment/route change expected to invalidate it.
- Sealdiver selection and Grapple/Dash traversal are current observed examples, not substitutes for the full matrix.

Close only when all rows pass on one compatible head, required dedicated-server/two-client and inspected user-path evidence exists, and the final V1 single-authority audit passes.

## 2026-09-07 Tiny3D alignment and production asset admission
Current cross-repo authority is organicoverlords/tiny3d, especially its northstar/design update #375, authoring #372, rigging benchmark #373 and proof #13. Historical TinyLab links below are provenance, not a separate current product owner.

P3 owns materialization, profile/AnimBP/gameplay binding, physics/runtime cost and actual proof; Tiny3D owns source preparation/rigging and portable motion. Use #394 as the consumer executor and #2610 for complete match-state animation.

Stock Fox is excluded from inputs, donors, roster/benchmarks, qualification and fallbacks. Do not substitute stock or primitive placeholders for required user/generated asset proof. Preserve actual selected asset/variant identity and existing valid source/package work; newer unqualified content is a gap, not an automatic replacement.

Admission should surface missing/LFS-pointer content, incompatible skeleton/clip/profile, wrong axes/scale/materials, physics/collision gap and stale content/build identity before an expensive runtime attempt. Reuse merged #2429 materialization enforcement rather than recreating it.

Return exact package/mission/job/object/clip/runtime identities and the complete readable retained proof bundle through #394. Offline Tiny3D acceptance, P3 diagnostic playback and actual Lane War gameplay remain distinct. Update only the evidence invalidated by the changed source/rig/motion/consumer/capture input.

---

Cross-repo product aim: organicoverlords/TinyLab#77
Newest-content intake: organicoverlords/TinyLab#84

P3 is the real consumer/proof side of the Tiny3D asset lifecycle. The newest viable production assets and characters must not stop at Tiny3D packaging; they must be materialized into current P3/V2 and used through the intended gameplay/runtime paths.

Acceptance:
- Consume selected newest production assets/characters from verified Tiny3D identities/handoffs rather than creating an unrelated P3-only lineage.
- Preserve Tiny3D asset ID, handoff/package SHA-256 and mission identity in P3 materialization/result evidence.
- Record exact Unreal object/package paths actually created, reused or intentionally bound: StaticMesh/SkeletalMesh, Skeleton, AnimSequences, PhysicsAsset, materials/data assets and role-specific bindings as applicable.
- Prefer newest viable production replacements for current required P3 roles; explicitly mark older replaced content historical/superseded rather than using it for final milestone proof.
- Character/creature selections must be exercised through current V2 spawn/animation/movement/gameplay paths where their role requires it.
- Static/building/environment selections must be exercised through their real P3 render/collision/placement/destruction/earthworks path where applicable.
- Player-visible proof must use a genuine current rendered frame from the intended V2 runtime/world and be registered through the normal P3 milestone capture path.
- Legacy/showroom/network-smoke-only execution cannot satisfy current V2 player-facing proof.
- Return attributable materialization/runtime result receipts to Tiny3D so the library can expose P3_MATERIALIZED / P3_RUNTIME_PROVEN / failure state for the same asset identity.

Newest-content gate:
- Before final acceptance, compare selected P3 assets against the current newest viable source/library assets.
- If a newer intended replacement exists but is not Tiny3D-qualified and P3-proven, report it as an explicit gap rather than claiming coverage complete.
- At minimum, prove the newest viable character/creature plus representative newest static/environment/building/prop assets actually required by P3.

This issue is complete only when the selected newest assets are both present as canonical Tiny3D library assets and actively materialized/tested in P3; either half alone is incomplete.


## Newest-150 P3 consumption gate

P3 must consume the Tiny3D newest-150 production dataset rather than only a few hand-picked examples. Every selected asset required by a live P3 role must preserve its Tiny3D identity through Unreal materialization. The Tiny3D animation classification controls what P3 must exercise: walking/flying/swimming gameplay locomotion, cloth/fabric motion, tentacle/tail/appendage motion, feather/wing motion, foliage wind, rigid articulation, destruction or genuinely static behavior as applicable. Player-visible classified motion requires current rendered proof; a successful static import cannot satisfy an animation-required contract.


## Deterministic automatic consumer contract

P3 consumption is part of the unattended lifecycle, not a manual import ceremony. Given the same verified Tiny3D handoff and P3 version/configuration, the consumer must deterministically materialize or reuse the same intended Unreal objects/bindings, run the same role-qualified validation mission, and return hash-bound materialization/runtime proof without routine human sequencing.

Ambiguous Tiny3D semantics remain explicit gaps and must not be guessed by P3. Independent valid assets continue. Player-visible proof still requires the normal real V2 rendered-runtime evidence; automation is not permission to substitute logs/headless checks for visual acceptance.

The 100-asset bundle at `G:\Oma Drive\LowVRAM3D_asset_bundle_20260814` (9 categories: birds, characters, other_animals, other_assets, other_things, plants ├ù20, random_items, rocks, trees) plus the 389 entries already in `Content/Showroom/Static` are the raw material for populating the Lane War world. This issue is the p3 side of that: consuming qualified assets, not producing them.

**Route: through Tiny3D, not straight into p3.** That is the documented product boundary ÔÇö LowVRAM produces geometry and provenance, Tiny3D owns compilation, validation, qualification and the library, p3 is the downstream consumer that materializes and accepts at runtime. Importing bundle GLBs directly into `Content/` would skip qualification and put unvalidated meshes into the world with no way to answer later whether they passed anything.

Depends on organicoverlords/tiny3d#101 (unified hash-indexed library) and the materialization identity contract in organicoverlords/tiny3d#12.

Scope here:

1. Take the qualified set Tiny3D hands back, by content hash, not by filename.
2. Materialize into `Content/` under the existing showroom convention, recording the exact object/package path per asset so the identity contract round-trips.
3. Place them in the world ÔÇö `Content/Showroom/Maps/ALL_ASSETS_Lineup.umap` is the existing lineup for review; Lane War placement is the actual goal (see #413 base structures, #414 battlefield, #416 creeps).
4. Import in batches with GC between assets ÔÇö a bulk GLB import loop inside the editor OOMs it.
5. Acceptance is a rendered frame through `scripts/Invoke-P3VisualProofCapture.ps1`, not an import log. Assets present in the content browser is not the same claim as assets visible in the world.

Note for provenance: 17 of the assets already in `Content/Showroom/Static` have no surviving master PLY (deleted 2026-08-23). They are usable in their materialized form, but they cannot be regenerated at a different resolution or face budget without re-running generation from the source image.

## 2026-09-07 contribution and delivery plan
Authority remains docs/v2/P3_V2_NORTH_STAR.md; detailed refinement: docs/v2/P3_PLAYABLE_MATCH_DIRECTION.md.

| Required result | Existing issue / mutation owner | Handoff / acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Join, play, finish, replay | #2442; existing session menu/launcher/match owner | Ordinary solo and LAN routes, two perspectives, clear failure/retry and clean rematch |
| Creep/terrain/defense counterplay | #2437/#2440 with #1012/#1033 | Real navigation changes after edit/build/destroy; no permanent route soft lock |
| Movement and readable combat | #2439/#2461, #2441/#1091 | Ski/grapple route affects a live fight; readable tells/impact in both views |
| Meaningful spending | #2438 | Earn -> choice -> visible lane consequence under authoritative economy |
| Full generated character motion | #2610, #331/#394, Tiny3D #372 | Current roster state/transition proof and exact returned asset attribution |
| Combined playability | #2611 | Fixed real-match workload, measured cost/budget and no visual/gameplay regression |
| Final user acceptance | #941 | One compatible build/content/configuration completes the normal-user match sequence |

Respect existing source WIP: #2605 placement, #2600 route rollback, #2603 wave phase and #2606 ski HUD are current review/integration candidates, not prompts for duplicate patches. File owners integrate overlapping contributions. P3LaneWarHUDWidget.cpp and P3TowerDefenseFeatureActor.cpp are shared serialization boundaries; different UI labels/checklists are not parallel source scopes.

### Priority and closure
Finish ready gameplay and the integrated user path before optional technology experiments or infra refinement. #599/#611 remain maintenance owners, not parent permission gates for #803. Use normal build/proof owners only to resolve a demonstrated blocker. The dated architecture program's lane/capacity observations are history, not current worker or machine state.

Use a single exact scenario/head/content set for normal launch -> join/solo -> fight/move -> reshape/build/destroy -> earn/spend -> win/loss -> replay. Existing source/contract passes are valuable but cannot close missing runtime or visual steps. Record the first unmet step and reuse still-valid proof.

No new product ledger, orchestrator or acceptance framework is needed: this issue and #941 remain the composition record. Design completion is not match completion.

---

Authority: `docs/v2/P3_V2_NORTH_STAR.md` (product thesis + immediate friend-playable priority; update in PR #802).
Parent/default-path acceptance: #611.
Existing component owners: #413 base/core assets, #414 battlefield, #205 character roster/animation, #206 earthworks+building+destruction, #331 qualified asset intake.

## Goal

Ship the first **friend-playable V2 Lane War** as one integrated multiplayer product slice, not a set of disconnected subsystem demos.

## Required match

- Two opposing teams/bases on the V2 production path.
- Each team visibly has **walls/defences + a base/house asset + a Core asset**.
- The Core is the heart/objective creeps and enemy players try to destroy and is server-authoritative/player-placeable or movable so the player can choose its defended position.
- A clear 3D road/lane connects the bases; ordinary creeps follow it toward the opposing Core.
- Players can construct additional defences around the Core and along the lane.
- Valid construction/earthworks/destruction change real traversal and creep navigation.

## Movement, combat and terrain

- Grappling hook, Tribes-style momentum skiing/surfing, earthworks, rapid building, destruction and spells/abilities all work in the same two-player match.
- Earthworks raises/lowers lane ground to create ramps/ski lines, berms, trenches/pits, high ground, blockers and creep reroutes.
- Destruction/counter-building can reopen or reshape routes.
- Creeps react to blockers/terrain rather than walking through meaningful changes.

## Economy

- Creep-related play and elapsed time award spendable gold.
- Gold can buy at minimum **additional allied creep/minion spawns** and upgrades that visibly affect the live Lane War.
- Gold, purchases, spawns and upgrades are server-authoritative and replicated.

## Characters and spells

- The chosen first playable roster is fully animated through real gameplay states: locomotion, skiing/traversal, grapple/air states where applicable, attacks/spells, defeat and respawn.
- Spells/abilities have readable cast/start, active/travel, impact/result and resource/cooldown feedback where applicable.
- No static/partially animated placeholder character counts for the milestone.

## Acceptance

1. Host can start a normal two-player session and a friend can join through a user-facing flow; developer-only PIE is not final acceptance.
2. Both players see complete opposing bases and the road/lane.
3. Creeps spawn, navigate, fight and damage the enemy Core.
4. Players fight with visible spells while using grapple/ski/high-mobility traversal.
5. Terrain or construction changes a creep/player route; destruction or counter-building changes it again.
6. Gold rises from creep-related play/time and can be spent on extra creep/minion spawns or an upgrade that changes the match.
7. Destroying a Core produces replicated match resolution.
8. Canonical reviewed visual proof shows both bases, creeps, full character animation, spells, terrain/build/destruction interaction, economy feedback and match resolution on one compatible head.
9. The user receives a practical launch/test path for playing with a friend plus representative proof media.

## Scope rule

Compose and finish existing V2 owners. Do not create duplicate movement, construction, earthworks, combat, Lane War or asset systems for this issue. This issue owns the integrated playable result and friend-test acceptance.

## 2026-09-07 integrated acceptance refinement
Execution plan lives in #803; no duplicate implementation scope here.

Use one compatible revision, executable/build, map/Experience, settings and selected content set. Preserve the existing base/Core/shop selections until a better qualified replacement is proven. Stock Fox is excluded; Tiny3D owns generated rigging.

Required normal-user sequence:
1. Start solo versus AI; separately host/join LAN with two real player perspectives. Say exactly which routes were tested; local two-instance proof does not establish Internet play.
2. Find the lane, opponent/Core, shop, controls and first useful action from normal UI without developer commands.
3. Fight with visible character/spell state; ski/grapple a useful route in both first-/third-person.
4. Edit terrain, place a defense and destroy/reopen it; observe the same collision/navigation result on both sides.
5. Earn and spend gold; see the changed lane pressure/upgrade effect.
6. Defeat/respawn and character swap preserve the declared state; Core defeat gives correct replicated result.
7. Rematch/restart/return through the existing UI; no leaked input, actors, timers, abilities, gold or old result state.

Attach a short chaptered normal-play sequence plus exact proof/trace references. Diagnostic close-ups supplement it for contact/deformation; they do not substitute for play. Independent review must inspect pixels, not only receipt fields. Retain raw evidence and exact content/package dependencies so replay survives relocation/link expiry.

Report incomplete steps honestly. #2610 owns missing full animation coverage; #2611 owns the measured combined workload. No new proof harness is requested.

---

Parent convergence issue: #803  ## What the user actually wants  A single playable V2 match that feels like a game, not a collection of disconnected systems.  ### Core match - **2 opposing bases**. - **1 clear road/lane** connecting them. - **Creeps spawn continuously** and travel down that road toward the enemy base/core. - Killing/playing around creeps and elapsed match play produces **gold**. - Gold can be spent on meaningful match actions/upgrades. - Playable as **1v1 versus AI** or **multiplayer 1v1**.  ### Terrain and routing - **Earthworks** must work during the match. - Players can raise/lower terrain, dig trenches, make ramps/berms/high ground, and otherwise reshape the battlefield. - Terrain edits must affect **real traversal**. - Terrain edits must also affect **creep routing**: creeps should reroute around blocked paths or follow newly viable paths instead of ignoring terrain changes.  ### Building and destruction - Players can **build defenses/walls/assets** around the base and lane. - These structures are **destructible**. - Destruction must visibly reopen or change routes. - Building + destruction + earthworks must all coexist in the same match and influence players/creeps rather than being separate demos.  ### Player movement and characters - **Tribes-style skiing/momentum** is usable in the real match. - **Grappling hook** works in the real match. - **Character swapping** works from a usable roster rather than a placeholder pawn. - Character swaps preserve a usable gameplay experience with correct scale/orientation/animation.  ### Combat and spells - The player has **skills/spells** in the match. - Spells must be visibly readable and functional, including the **meteor** path. - Spells interact with the actual battlefield/enemies rather than only appearing in a proof/demo path.  ## Required integrated experience  The intended result is:  > Spawn into a 1v1 match, choose/swap a character, move with normal controls + skiing + grapple, fight using spells, earn gold from lane play, build and destroy defenses, reshape the terrain with earthworks, and watch creeps reroute through the changed battlefield while two bases fight across one clear road/lane.  This should work in either **player vs AI** or **player vs player** form.  ## Acceptance  Do not call this complete because individual source systems, unit tests, or isolated PIE probes pass. The normal user launch must visibly prove on one compatible head:  1. Two visible opposing bases and one readable connecting road/lane. 2. Creeps spawn, move down the lane, fight, and target the opposing base/core. 3. Gold increases from creep/match play and is spendable. 4. 1v1 works against AI and multiplayer 1v1 remains supported. 5. Earthworks visibly changes terrain during the match. 6. Creeps reroute when terrain/building changes block or alter their route. 7. Building works and placed walls/assets are destructible. 8. Destruction visibly changes traversal/routing again. 9. Skiing is real momentum/slope movement, not a short dash. 10. Grappling hook is visibly usable in the real match. 11. Character swapping works with correctly scaled/oriented/animated characters. 12. Spells/skills work, including meteor, with visible cast/impact/result. 13. All of the above is tested through the same ordinary human-facing launch path, not disconnected developer-only demos.  ## Non-goal  Do not rebuild duplicate systems that already exist. Converge the existing V2/Tiny3D/gameplay work into this one playable result and fix missing runtime bindings/assets/presentation where they prevent the experience above. 
### Base composition must use the user's real assets
- Each side must have a visibly composed **base area**, not a floating/default pawn in an empty map.
- The **Core must use the user's intended Core asset(s)** already selected for V2; primitive placeholders or generic dummy meshes do not count.
- Each base must visibly include the previously required **house/base structure, surrounding wall/defence pieces, shop, Core, and readable base dressing**.
- The shop must be a real visible/interactable part of the base/economy loop, not only a hidden actor or code path.
- The road/lane must physically and visually connect the two completed bases.
- Existing user assets already admitted through P3/Tiny3D should be used where they are the intended product assets. Do not replace them with temporary cubes, mannequins, untextured stand-ins, or invisible actors for acceptance.
- Scale, orientation, materials/textures and placement must be visibly correct in the normal launch. A giant sideways character, floating pawn, missing material, or off-map asset is a failure.

P3AnimationProfile.h is a shared core contract: change it only for a demonstrated missing interface, separately from feature/content edits.

## Problem
The current profile supports AnimBP and idle/locomotion/airborne fallbacks plus cosmetic melee, but that structure alone cannot prove the full match roster animates correctly while skiing, grappling, casting, swapping, dying and respawning. The milestone requires those real behaviors, not renamed or idle-only clips.

## Acceptance
- Use a small explicit selected generated roster, with exact Tiny3D source/package/skeleton/clip identities; stock Fox is excluded entirely. Missing source/motion goes back to Tiny3D, not a P3 rig-generation implementation.
- Publish a state/transition matrix for idle/start/stop/turn/run, skiing, grapple/air/landing, action/cast, hit reaction when supported, defeat/respawn and character swap. Required/optional/unsupported are explicit.
- Existing gameplay state selects motion; no arbitrary timer showcase or root/camera-only motion can satisfy it.
- Contacts, stride/speed, authored scale/orientation, sockets and weapon grip remain coherent; no runtime 0.01 or yaw repair.
- Declare root-motion ownership, locomotion/action/additive masks, cancellation, contact/notify windows and IK adjustments. Cosmetic animation notifies must not become authoritative damage or purchases.
- Swap and respawn preserve intended player state and remove obsolete pawn animation/ability/camera bindings. Verify held input, interrupted cast/grapple and late client observation.
- Prove two compatible generated characters by profile/content reuse rather than a new base-class branch; then show the selected milestone roster's actual coverage.
- First-person preserves aim and essential tells; third-person makes body motion readable. Observer sees the same gameplay result even if animation sampling differs.
- A short diagnostic close-up makes contacts/deformation inspectable; actual Lane War footage proves gameplay. Bind trace/active clip/time and media to the same execution; use #394 and existing review owners.

## Technology decision
Start with the current AnimBP/profile baseline plus scripted IK retargeting and targeted IK/contact repair. Compare Pose Search/Motion Matching only if eligible clip coverage and measured transition quality justify it. Motion Warping may align a bounded authored action to a declared target; it cannot replace server movement/hit authority. Use Rewind Debugger/Animation Insights to explain bad transitions. Parent #803 / #941. This is a game performance and tuning issue, not build/fleet/infrastructure work.

| Contribution | Existing owner / exact boundary | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fixed playable workload | Existing Lane War P3Testing scenario; issue-owned evidence result | Versioned normal-match scenario/input recipe and observed baseline |
| Navigation/terrain costs | Existing P3Earthworks + P3AI/P3TowerDefense owners; each concrete .cpp serial with #1012/#2437/#2440 | Fix only measured collision/nav/game-thread hotspot; preserve route correctness |
| Animation/VFX/render cost | P3AvatarHumanoid, P3CombatMeteorPresentationActor.cpp and exact existing content assets | Bounded quality/cost change preserving readable attacks/contacts |
| Independent replay/review | Existing Unreal Insights, runtime and capture tools | Same-workload before/after trace and reviewed video; immutable head and settings |

The first contributor pins the workload through this issue, not a new registry. Others reuse that baseline and select a proven independent hotspot; they do not each build another profiler or benchmark harness.

## Uncovered acceptance
Subsystem passes do not show that two players, creeps, meteor/spells, construction/destruction and earthworks coexist without severe hitches or unreadable effects. Establish a measured combined-match budget and fix the worst load-bearing failure.

## Scope
- Use the normal selected Lane War map, roster, view/resolution/quality, machine/build identity, creep/wave counts, edit/placement/destruction sequence and spell activity. Keep cold launch separate from warmed play.
- Measure client frame-time p50/p95/p99, game/render/GPU time, server frame/update time, peak RAM/VRAM, nav/collision completion latency, animation/VFX load and obvious repeated hitch/stall counts with existing Unreal Insights/stat tools.
- Use the existing Earthworks contract of no single >100 ms game-thread hitch over 30 standard edits; retain its recorded p95 requirement. Choose and record a reference hardware/quality tier and overall frame target from the first real baseline before tuning. Do not invent a current FPS result.
- Verify both first/third-person and host/remote-client behavior at the chosen bounded workload. Frame budgets are measured acceptance for that configuration, not hardware-dependent unit-test thresholds.
- Prioritize playable responsiveness, visible attack/impact cues, contact quality and prompt correct navigation. Reduce unnecessary work before reducing essential readability.
- Profile animation budget/update-rate controls, VFX scalability/culling and bounded nav tile regeneration only where a trace identifies the cost. Far-away animation throttling must not break gameplay notifies/contacts; nav generation must retain a complete Core route.
- Repeat the same workload once after the targeted change; expand only to answer a concrete regression question. Preserve raw trace and proof references; do not create recurring performance workers.

## Done
A declared reproducible workload has an honest baseline, reference-tier budget, measured correction for its dominant failing cost, and independently reviewed normal-match evidence without gameplay/visual regression. If already within budget, publish that measured result and stop optimization.
